title: She Had 34 Seconds to Save Her Children. She Couldn't Save All Three.
description:
On the evening of May 6th, 1937, Matilde Doehner was sitting in the dining room of the Hindenburg with her three children. In twelve minutes, the air outside the windows would catch fire.

What followed has been recreated from the Doehner family's own surviving accounts, period photographs, and the official Lakehurst investigation records. This is what the disaster looked like from inside the ship — from one family's table in the dining room, in the thirty-four seconds it took for the Hindenburg to reach the ground.

If this kind of history stays with you, subscribe — we rebuild the last hours of people history remembers, one frame at a time.
